images.title: Four right angles force equal opposite sides
images.purpose: Shows quadrilateral ABCD with four right angles split by diagonal BD into two congruent triangles, so its opposite sides are equal.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rectangle in the centre, cut by one diagonal into two lightly shaded triangles, with the equal sides marked.
images.exact_structure: One quadrilateral ABCD in dark outline, wider than tall, with A top left, B top right, C bottom right and D bottom left. A small square right angle mark sits in each of the four corners; the marks at A and C are filled reddish purple (#CC79A7), the marks at B and D are plain outline. The diagonal BD is a dark line from top right to bottom left. Triangle BAD (top left) is lightly filled teal (#0072B2) and triangle DCB (bottom right) is lightly filled amber (#E69F00). Sides AD and CB each carry one short tick mark; sides AB and DC each carry two short tick marks. Under the shape, centred, the line ∆BAD ≅ ∆DCB. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Four right angles are enough: the diagonal makes two congruent triangles, so opposite sides are equal.
images.description: Shows quadrilateral ABCD with four right angles split by diagonal BD into two congruent triangles, so its opposite sides are equal.
images.context: AAS: ∠A = ∠C = 90°, BD common, ∠ABD = ∠CDB (each 90° − ∠DBC). Matching order B to D, A to C, D to B.

image_decisions.why: The two shaded triangles with matching right angles show why four right angles give equal opposite sides.
